Search title+author, resolve concrete PDF files through item metadata, then validate with qpdf.
Use edition/work metadata and availability to locate Internet Archive identifiers; do not bulk-download Open Library data.
Arabic Collections Online explicitly describes its collection as public-domain Arabic content and provides low/high-resolution PDF downloads; verify exact work/edition before acquisition.
Use digitized Arabic/Islamic manuscripts where the individual record explicitly states CC0/Public Domain or equivalent permission; PDF and image downloads are available on qualifying records.
Use only file records with an explicit compatible/public-domain license; preserve the file page and license evidence.
Use scanned editions and PDF files only when the file record provides an explicit public-domain/open-license basis.

Global index spanning major Arabic/Islamic manuscript collections; follow each record to the holding library and acquire only where the holding source permits download/use.

Metadata cross-check only; especially useful for modern editions and identifiers, not as a primary Arabic heritage PDF source.

manuscript_policy: A digitized manuscript is acquired as a book-level review object when a complete or materially complete digital surrogate is available. OCR may be generated for search, but OCR never replaces the manuscript images as the authoritative witness.
public_policy: Only records with explicit verified redistribution permission may become public downloadable PDFs. Review-only or rights-unclear copies remain encrypted and source-linked.
forbidden_shortcut: Never persist a discovery URL as an acquired book. An acquired record requires an actual validated PDF or complete permitted scan.
